feature.title: Masks
feature.summary: Keep the pattern. Give the melody a mind of its own.
feature.prose: Patterns supply the material; a channel merges it; masks give you the last word on individual attributes. Change a note without disturbing its rhythm, tuck in a quiet accent, or add a chord above a bass line.
feature.musical_use: Start with a two-note motif. Repeat its contour, then change the last note on every second phrase. Use velocity for emphasis before adding more notes.

details.title: Read X as inherit
details.text: X is an unset attribute, not zero. A step's explicit attribute wins over the channel default; an unset step uses the default; an unset default falls back to merged pattern data. Clearing step overrides does not erase the defaults.

details.title: Chords need a polyphonic output
details.text: Chd1–Chd4 are four additional scale-relative voices above or below the root. 3rd and 5th are intervals, not MIDI note numbers. Start with one added voice; use strum and chord velocity for separation.

details.title: Scale, degree and rotation
details.text: By default, note masks snap to the chosen scale. They do not follow degree or rotation unless full quantisation is enabled. Snap Note Masks to Scale, Quantise Note Masks and the Fully Quantise Mask trig parameter interact; the existing M-MASK-019–021 cases cover this precedence.

details.title: MIDI and clearing
details.text: Hold a step and play a MIDI keyboard to enter notes and chords. Live recording is another route. A held step takes precedence over channel-wide clearing even with K1 down. Other channels are unaffected. The existing suite checks steps 63/64, multiple chord slots and recorded-chord clearing.

details.title: If a new note is silent
details.text: Check the selected channel's output, active range and mute state. A trig alone needs an audible note, velocity and length. A mono voice cannot sound all chord voices together. To undo an exception, hold that step and press K2.

details.title: Why the screen calls MIDI 60 C3
details.text: Mosaic uses the norns musicutil octave convention: floor(MIDI note / 12 − 2). MIDI 60 is therefore displayed as C3. Many other instruments call that same pitch C4; the numeric MIDI note is unchanged. Recipes here use the names shown on norns.

recipes.title: A melody that answers itself
recipes.text: Use C major. Write C5–D5–G5–E5 on steps 1, 4, 7 and 11 of a 16-step lead channel. On the next phrase, replace E5 with D5, then resolve to C5. Keep the first three attacks unchanged so the listener recognises the motif.

recipes.title: Ghost notes and syncopation
recipes.text: Keep the main accent at velocity 90. Add a half-step note just before it at velocity 35. Once the contrast works, use Trig Probability on the quiet note for occasional surprises. Lower velocity makes a ghost note; probability decides whether it happens.

recipes.title: A harmony with room to breathe
recipes.text: Put long C3 notes on a bass channel and C4 roots with 3rd and 5th chord masks on a polyphonic channel. Move one chord voice by the smallest available scale interval for voice leading. A B4 lead note adds tension; resolve it to C5. Keep drum kit note mapping separate from pitched harmony.

recipes.title: Let the loop lengths disagree
recipes.text: Keep drums at 16 steps and try a five-step masked melody. Their starts meet again after 80 steps. Add swing on the channel Clock page for a lilt; compare before combining swing with shuffle. These are adjacent-feature recipes, not new mask controls.

scenes.title: Give one step its own melody

steps.caption: Open Channel tasks with E1. Turn E2 to Masks and press K3. Select Note with E2.
Turn E3 to G3 with no step held. This is the channel default; the original rhythm and velocities stay.
Hold step 1, then turn E3 five detents. C4 belongs to this step, above the G3 default.
Release step 1. The screen returns to the G3 channel default; playback keeps the C4 exception.
Give step 2 a D4 exception, then release it. Two different notes now sit on the same default.
Hold step 1 and press K2. Release it. Its exception disappears; step 2 still plays D4.
With no grid keys held, hold K1 and press K2. All step exceptions clear; G3 remains the channel default.
Open Masks and select Vel. X means inherit the pattern's velocity.
Set a channel velocity of 50. Every note is softer; pitch and timing are inherited.
Hold step 1 and raise its velocity to 90. Release it: the accent survives, with no pitch change.
Hold step 2 and turn E3 down to 0. Zero is a silent velocity, distinct from the X inheritance state.
Release step 2, then hold it again and press K2. Release it: the channel velocity 50 returns.
Select Len and turn E3 to a half-step gate. The short envelope leaves room between notes.

scenes.title: Turn four notes into a small harmony

steps.caption: Open Masks and select Chd1. The four chord slots add voices to the root.
Turn E3 two detents to 3rd. These are scale-relative intervals, not absolute MIDI note numbers.
Hold step 1 and move its Chd1 from 3rd to 5th. Only this step opens out to C–G.
Release step 1. The screen shows the channel 3rd again, while the first chord remains a fifth.
Hold step 1 and press K2, then release. The fifth is gone and the default thirds return.

scenes.title: Add a note where the pattern is empty

steps.caption: Open Masks. Our source has four notes and four empty steps in an eight-step loop.
Set Note to C3, Vel to 80 and Len to a half-step. These defaults make a new trig audible.
Hold K1 and tap step 5. A forced-on trig adds an extra C3 after the source's four notes.
Repeat K1 + step 5 to remove that note. The original four-note rhythm continues.

audio.title: Small hours · four bars in C major
audio.description: Four bars in C major: a Polyperc bass answers soft Doubledecker chords. The bass moves from C to G and back; scale-relative 3rd and 5th masks turn the chord roots into harmony. Two independent channels leave space between attacks.
